h1: Rockgarden Beach Resort Rayong — Beachside Garden Bungalow Resort in Laem Mae Phim
intro: Picture a resort that isn't a tall beachfront block but a scattering of bungalows across a big, green, shady garden, with a pool that has a slide for the kids, where you walk through the garden and come out onto a quiet stretch of sand with almost no one on it — Rockgarden Beach Resort is a resort in the Laem Mae Phim area, Tambon Kram, Klaeng District, Rayong, laid out across roughly 300 rai of beachside garden · What real reviews praise here is the wide, shady garden, the pool with a slide, the quiet private beach, and the very low price, starting at about ฿1,500/night · But we have to be honest from the start: this is a resort where reviews split clearly into two camps — some people love the quiet and the value, while TripAdvisor gives it just 2.2 out of 5 from 11 reviews, with complaints about upkeep, cleanliness, and an atmosphere so quiet it can feel deserted · This review covers both sides plainly so you can decide whether the place suits your style of stay.

body.html: Overview — who Rockgarden Beach Resort is for — To put it as simply as possible, Rockgarden Beach Resort is a bungalow resort in a beachside garden that trades mainly on the words "quiet" and "budget-friendly" · It isn't a luxury beachfront resort with brand-new buildings and five-star service, and it isn't a city hotel where everything is a short walk away · It's standalone-bungalow accommodation scattered across a large garden of roughly 300 rai in the Laem Mae Phim area, Tambon Kram, Klaeng District, a stretch of coast that is still calm and not as busy as Rayong's main beaches · From real reviews on both Trip.com and TripAdvisor, the clear picture is that the people who "fit" here are budget travelers who aren't fussy about how new the rooms are, who want a wide space for the kids to run around, a pool to splash in, and a quiet beach for an evening walk, treating the resort as a place to sleep and unwind rather than somewhere to soak up service · Meanwhile, the people who "don't fit" are those who want spotless rooms, service on hand at all times, or a lively atmosphere with activities, because many reviews agree that the place is so quiet it can sometimes look empty · The low price here therefore comes with the need to set the right expectations — think of it as a camp-style stay close to nature by the sea, rather than a resort polished in every corner.

Location and getting there — Rockgarden Beach Resort sits at Moo 6, Tambon Kram, Klaeng District, Rayong, in a zone many people loosely call the Laem Mae Phim area · Its location highlight is that it is right on a private beach, with Nam Daeng Beach only about 0.4 km away — you can walk straight through the garden out to the sea · If you want Mae Phim Beach, the main beach with more seafood restaurants and a livelier feel, it's about 3.8 km away, a few minutes by car · Laem Tan Pier, used to catch boats to nearby islands, is about 2.7 km away · The advantage of this location is the quiet and privacy, since it's away from the main tourist strip, but the trade-off you have to accept is that getting around relies mainly on having your own car · There are no convenience stores or restaurants within walking distance of the resort, so anyone without a car will struggle to find food and get out and about · It's about 40–50 min by car from Rayong town, and from Bangkok it's about three and a half to four hours via the motorway and the Rayong–Klaeng highway · We'd suggest bringing some supplies and drinking water yourself, since the resort restaurant keeps limited hours.

"I really loved how quiet it is here. The garden is huge and you can stroll around all day, the kids had a blast on the pool slide, and the beach was quiet with almost no one on it · But you do need your own car, because there's nothing around — you have to drive out to Mae Phim Beach to eat."

Room types and decor — The rooms at Rockgarden Beach Resort are bungalows and rooms in low-rise buildings scattered through the garden, not a single tall block · The room types found on booking channels are the Superior and Deluxe groups, many of them designed to sleep up to 4, which suits families or groups of friends · Inside, the decor is simple, leaning on being practical rather than luxurious, with air conditioning, a fridge, a TV, and a private bathroom with a water heater and shower · Some rooms have garden views; some sit closer to the sea · The point we have to put plainly is that the condition of the rooms is what reviews talk about most, and it cuts both ways · Those who were happy say they got an air-conditioned bungalow with Wi-Fi and hot water for a few hundred to just over a thousand baht, which counts as more than worth it · But those who were disappointed in TripAdvisor reviews mention damp, musty smells, peeling paint, old furniture, hard beds, and fridges that don't work in some rooms · This is why we'd suggest you see the room before you actually check in if you can, and not expect the standard of a freshly renovated resort · If you view it as a simple place near the sea to sleep after a full day in the water, it's acceptable, but if clean, new rooms are your top priority, this may not be the answer.

Facilities, pool and beach — The highlight that keeps people speaking well of Rockgarden Beach Resort is its spacious common areas · The outdoor pool with a slide is what families with kids love most, and there's a separate kids' pool so little ones can play safely · Around the pool and throughout the resort is a large, shady garden, which many reviews praise as somewhere you can stroll, cycle, or let the kids run around freely in plenty of space · Beyond that is a quiet private beach, better suited to evening walks and photos than to busy water activities · There's also a billiards room and ping-pong table for downtime, a BBQ area, fishing service, bicycle and car rental, and free parking across the wide grounds · The caveat to flag from real reviews is that the upkeep of the facilities is inconsistent — some reviews say the pool is clean and well kept, while at other times people complain that the pool wasn't cleaned, the poolside chairs were broken, or the bicycle tires were flat · This shows the experience can differ depending on the season and how many staff are on hand, so it's worth asking the resort about current conditions before you book.

Food and the on-site restaurant — Food is something to set the right expectations for from the start · Rockgarden Beach Resort has an on-site restaurant, but from the information and real reviews, it operates fairly limited hours — at times it serves only breakfast, and some reviews even say the restaurant looks like it isn't fully up and running · The policy on some booking channels states "breakfast not included" for certain rooms, while others say it is included, so it's worth checking the terms clearly when you book · For this reason, most guests choose to drive out to eat, especially at Mae Phim Beach, which has several seafood and made-to-order restaurants a few minutes' drive away · Another option many families pick is to use the resort's BBQ area, buying fresh seafood to grill themselves in the garden, which fits the place's seaside camp feel · In short, food is not the resort's strong point, and you shouldn't rely on the on-site restaurant — plan your meals in advance and bring supplies or plan to drive out from the start.

Service — Service at Rockgarden Beach Resort is another point where reviews split clearly into two sides · On the positive side, many praise the staff as friendly, kind, and willing to help, and even though some speak limited English, they're happy to look after guests · The caveat is around how many staff there are and when someone is on duty — some reviews say there are barely any staff early in the morning before eight, and at times the resort looks quiet, as if no one is fully in charge · This is a reflection of a large resort that may have a small team relative to its grounds · The honest advice is that if you're someone who wants service available around the clock, or immediate help with everything, this place may leave you feeling a little short-changed · But if you're self-sufficient, have a car, and are looking for a quiet place to unwind, this level of service is fine for what you pay · We'd suggest contacting the resort directly in advance to confirm your booking and ask about check-in and check-out, to avoid arriving with no one there to receive you.

What real reviews say (both praise and criticism) — Pulling together Trip.com, TripAdvisor, and various booking channels, the picture is a resort that people "either really love or really hate" · On the praise side: a wide, shady garden you can stroll all day, a pool with a slide the kids love, a quiet and very private beach, a very low price for an air-conditioned beachside bungalow, and staff who are mostly friendly · There are reviews saying they got an air-conditioned bungalow with Wi-Fi and hot water for a few hundred baht, which counts as a steal for anyone on a tight budget · On the caveat side: this is the part that has to be stated clearly, because TripAdvisor gives an overall score of just 2.2 out of 5 from 11 reviews and places it near the bottom of Rayong's table · Common complaints are about upkeep — damp, musty smells, peeling paint, old and broken furniture, hard beds, with some reviews mentioning room and pool cleanliness at certain times, plus an atmosphere so quiet that some people feel the resort is deserted · These criticisms aren't minor, and they're the reason we put special weight on setting expectations and checking conditions before booking for this place.

"The price really is low and the garden really is lovely — the kids loved the pool · But the room we got had a slightly musty smell and some things were old, so you have to make a bit of peace with that · If you come without high expectations and bring your own car, it's fine for the price."

Price and value comparison — Rates at Rockgarden Beach Resort start at about ฿1,500/night, with an average in the range of around ฿2,500–2,900 depending on the room type and season · Some older reviews mention air-conditioned bungalow rates as low as a few hundred baht in low season · This is one of the cheapest price brackets among Rayong's beachside accommodation · Compared with other beachfront resorts in the Mae Phim–Klaeng zone, which usually start around ฿2,000–3,000 and up, Rockgarden has the edge on price and on much wider grounds · But the value here has to be measured from the right angle — you're paying little in exchange for space, quiet, and privacy, not for new rooms or full-service amenities · If you can accept simple rooms and inconsistent upkeep, this price is worth it for a budget seaside getaway · But if spending a little more gets a better-kept resort, for some people that may be more worth it in terms of peace of mind, so it's worth comparing prices with other options in the same area before you decide.

What to know before booking — This is a resort where preparing in advance can make a big difference · One, you should have your own car, because there are no restaurants or convenience stores within walking distance of the resort — you have to drive out to Mae Phim Beach to find food · Two, bring some supplies and drinking water yourself, since the resort restaurant keeps limited hours · Three, check the room's condition at check-in — if you get a room with a musty smell or in poor shape, ask to change immediately, and take photos for evidence · Four, contact the resort directly in advance to confirm your booking and check-in time, because there are reviews of arriving and struggling to find staff, especially outside office hours · Five, if you bring kids, the pool and garden are the main draw, but keep a close eye on children around the pool and slide · Six, choose a free-cancellation booking first if you're not sure yet, and always read the latest reviews before booking, because the condition of a resort like this can change depending on the upkeep at any given time.

Verdict — From all the real reviews, Rockgarden Beach Resort suits budget travelers with their own car who are looking for quiet, wide space, and a private seaside beach at a low price, without being fussy about how new and tidy the rooms are · The large garden of roughly 300 rai, the pool with a slide, and the quiet beach are draws that are hard to find at this price, and the reason some families come back to stay again · But it has to be said plainly that this place has caveats around upkeep, cleanliness, and inconsistent service, clearly reflected in its TripAdvisor score of 2.2 out of 5 · If you want spotless rooms, service on hand at all times, or a lively atmosphere with activities, this may not be the answer, and you should consider a better-kept resort in the Mae Phim or Ban Phe area instead · But if you understand that you're paying for space and privacy by the sea at a budget price, come well prepared, check the room's condition first, and set the right expectations — Rockgarden Beach Resort can be an option that meets what you want from a quiet seaside getaway in its own way.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Rockgarden Beach Resort Rayong

faq.q: Where is Rockgarden Beach Resort, and how do you get there?
faq.a: The resort is at Moo 6, Tambon Kram, Klaeng District, Rayong, in the Laem Mae Phim area · It's on a private beach, near Nam Daeng Beach (about 0.4 km), Laem Tan Pier (about 2.7 km) and Mae Phim Beach (about 3.8 km) · You should have your own car, because there are no restaurants or convenience stores within walking distance of the resort · It's about 40–50 min by car from Rayong town.

faq.q: What are Rockgarden Beach Resort's starting rates, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Rates start at about ฿1,500/night, with an average of around ฿2,500–2,900 depending on the room and season · Rooms are bungalows and Superior/Deluxe rooms in the garden, many sleeping up to 4, with air conditioning, a fridge and hot water — good for families on a budget.

faq.q: Who is Rockgarden Beach Resort for?
faq.a: It suits budget travelers with their own car who are looking for quiet, wide space, and a private seaside beach at a low price · It has a large garden, a pool with a slide, and a quiet beach · If you want spotless, new rooms, service on hand at all times, or a lively atmosphere, a better-kept resort in the Mae Phim or Ban Phe area may suit you more.

faq.q: What are the rooms and cleanliness at Rockgarden like?
faq.a: Reviews split clearly into two sides · Those who were happy say it's good value for an air-conditioned beachside bungalow · The caveats in TripAdvisor (2.2 out of 5 from 11 reviews) mention damp, musty smells, peeling paint, old furniture, and cleanliness at certain times · We'd suggest you check the room's condition at check-in and ask to change immediately if it's not okay, and read the latest reviews before booking.

faq.q: Is there a restaurant at the resort?
faq.a: There is an on-site restaurant, but it operates limited hours and at times serves only breakfast · Most guests choose to drive out to eat at Mae Phim Beach, which has several seafood restaurants, or use the resort's BBQ area, buying seafood to grill themselves · You should bring supplies and plan your meals in advance.

faq.q: Is there a pool and activities for kids?
faq.a: There's an outdoor pool with a slide and a separate kids' pool, which is what families talk about most · There's also a wide garden for kids to run around, a billiards and ping-pong room, fishing service, and bicycle rental · Keep a close eye on children around the pool and slide.
